# DATASET - credit-risk-pd (synthetic, seeded, 100 % generated by `python -m src.data.make_dataset`)

**Story.** 1,500 retail customers (current account + personal loan; about 84 % also have a credit card) observed for **54 months** (2021-01 .. 2025-06).
Every month-end a bank scores *existing* customers: "will this customer default (**90+ days past due**) within the **next 6 months**?"
A macro stress period starts in 2023-09 (fewer salary credits, higher card utilisation, more job-loss defaults, higher default hazard).

> Not real data. The numbers are plausible for teaching, not facts about any bank. About 34 % of the 1,500 customers default at some point in 54 months
> (a real bank would see a few percent per year) - this is deliberately high so that every monthly snapshot has enough positives (about 4 % of snapshot rows) to learn from.
> The brief asked for ~24 months of history; we simulate 54 so that train / purge / validation / test / production periods exist with 6-month label lags.

Regenerate: `python -m src.data.make_dataset` (5 s) then `python -m src.features.build_features` (10 s). Seed and sizes live in `params.yaml` (`data:`).

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 1. Raw tables (what core-banking systems deliver) - `data/raw/`

### customers.csv (1,500 rows, one per customer)
| column | type | meaning | allowed as a model input? |
|---|---|---|---|
| customer_id | int | key | NO - an identifier would let a tree memorise customers (also personal data) |
| signup_date | date | when the account was opened (1998 .. 2023) | only through `account_age` (months, derived) |
| segment | text: mass / affluent / small_business | customer segment | **NO - Rejected in the registry**: sensitive / proxy attribute (small_business customers have irregular income by construction); would also raise fairness questions |
| loan_amount | float INR | size of the personal loan | not used (the instalment burden is already visible in `loan_payment_ratio`) |
| loan_start_date | date | first month of the 84-month loan | used only inside `loan_payment_ratio` (how many payments were due) |
| credit_limit | float INR, **empty = no credit card** | card limit | used only inside `credit_utilization` (denominator) |

### transactions.csv (~324,000 rows, one per account movement)
| column | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| customer_id | int | key |
| txn_date | date | posting date; **available the same day** (availability lag 0) |
| amount | float INR, > 0 | absolute amount |
| txn_type | salary_credit / loan_payment / debit / credit_card_spend / atm / other_credit | what happened. Credits: salary_credit, other_credit. Debits: loan_payment, debit, atm. `credit_card_spend` is a memo line (card purchases do not move the current-account balance) |
| balance_after | float INR | current-account balance after this movement (can be negative) |

### loan_status.csv (~75,000 rows, one per customer-month once an instalment is due)
| column | type | meaning | usable at prediction time? |
|---|---|---|---|
| customer_id, month | key | month-end the status refers to | |
| days_past_due | int 0..180 | 30 x number of consecutive missed instalments (3 in a row = 90 = **default**) | only for months already published |
| missed_payment | 0/1 | the instalment of that month was not paid (or the account is frozen) | only for published months (feature `missed_payment_count`) |
| available_at | date | **month-end + 5 days**: the row is published on day 5 of the next month | this IS the availability rule |
| collections_status | none / arrears / in_collections | `in_collections` once dpd >= 90 | **LEAK**: set after default |
| recovery_amount | float | money recovered after default | **LEAK**: exists only after default |

### defaults.csv (1,500 rows)
| column | meaning |
|---|---|
| customer_id | key |
| default_date | month-end of the 3rd consecutive missed instalment; **empty = never defaults**. Used ONLY to build the label (the future) and to remove already-defaulted customers from later snapshots. Never a feature |

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 2. Snapshot dataset - `data/processed/snapshots.csv` (49,764 rows)
One row per (customer_id, as_of_date) for every month-end 2021-06-30 .. 2024-12-31 (6 months of history are needed before the first snapshot, and the last label needs 6 months after).
**Eligible** = signed up, >= 6 months of history, **not already in default** at as_of.

| column | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| customer_id, as_of_date | key | the **prediction timestamp** is `as_of_date` |
| 9 base features | float | see section 3 |
| default_next_6m | 0/1 | **target** = default_date in (as_of, as_of + 6 months] |
| split | text | time-based: train 2021-06..2022-03 / purge 2022-04..2022-08 / val 2022-09..2022-11 / test 2022-12..2023-02 / production 2023-03..2024-12 |

3 derived features (`util_x_missed`, `balance_trend_norm`, `log_average_balance`) are added by `add_derived_features()` - the same function in training, batch scoring and the API.

Why a **purge** period: the label of a train row (as_of 2022-03-31) is only known on 2022-09-30. A validation period starting right after train would use labels that did not exist when the model was built, and neighbouring months have overlapping label windows.

## 3. Features (all computed ONLY from rows with `available_at <= as_of_date`)
| feature | window | formula | missing when | allowed? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| average_balance | 90 days | mean(balance_after) | never | yes (v2; v1 was the leaky version - Rejected) |
| balance_trend | 6 months | OLS slope of 6 month-end balances | never | yes |
| salary_credit_frequency | 6 months | salary credits / 6 | never | yes |
| loan_payment_ratio | 6 months | payments made / payments due | never | yes |
| missed_payment_count | 6 published months | sum(missed_payment) | never | yes (availability lag 5 days) |
| credit_utilization | 6 months | mean monthly card spend / credit_limit | **no card** (~16 %) | yes |
| recent_transaction_count | 30 days | number of transactions | never | yes |
| income_stability | 6 months | std / mean of salary amounts | fewer than 2 salary credits | yes |
| account_age | static | months since signup | never | yes (vetoed by the out-of-time check, so not used by the model) |
| util_x_missed | derived | credit_utilization x missed_payment_count | no card | yes |
| balance_trend_norm | derived | clip(balance_trend / (abs(average_balance) + 1), -1, 1) | never | yes |
| log_average_balance | derived | log1p(max(average_balance, 0)) | never | yes |

Full metadata (owner, availability, status, lifecycle history): `configs/feature_registry.yaml`, printed with `python -m src.governance.feature_lifecycle table`.

### Features that exist ONLY to teach leakage (all Rejected in the registry)
| name | what it does | why it leaks |
|---|---|---|
| average_balance_leaky (v1) | mean balance of the 90 days up to the **extract date** = as_of + 7 months | includes the post-default balance collapse |
| dpd_target_period | max days_past_due inside the 6-month target window | default is *defined* as 90+ dpd, so this IS the label |
| recoveries_target_period | recoveries collected inside the target window | recoveries exist only after a default |
| collections_status_latest | collections status in the latest extract | set after the outcome |

## 4. Production batches - `data/production/` (columns = API request fields + `default_next_6m`)
| file | as_of | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| batch_normal.csv | 2023-03-31 | calm month; the "everything is fine" example (contains one significant-but-small drift: account_age) |
| batch_drifted.csv | 2024-01-31 | stress month: salary_credit_frequency down, credit_utilization up, income_stability worse, balance_trend down |
| batch_dq_issue.csv | 2023-03-31 | the calm month again, but ~38 % of `salary_credit_frequency` is empty (source-system migration): a **data-quality** problem, not drift |

`default_next_6m` is included so performance can be measured later. In real life it arrives **6 months after as_of** - until then performance is unknown.

`data/processed/reference.csv` = 2,000 random rows of the TRAINING snapshots (12 model features): the reference distribution for the KS test.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 5. Real-world problems injected (and where to see them)
| problem | how it is injected | where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| **Missing values (MAR)** | `credit_limit` empty for customers without a card; probability depends on segment (affluent 2 %, mass 22 %, small business 11 %) | `01_data_profile` section 3: `credit_utilization` 16 % missing |
| **Missing values (MNAR)** | `income_stability` undefined with < 2 salary credits: the customer has stopped receiving a salary, which *is* the risk | rare in calm months (3 training rows), more common under stress; pipeline keeps a missing indicator |
| **Class imbalance** | ~4 % of snapshots are positives (6 % in production) | `01_data_profile` section 2; why we use PR-AUC / recall@10 % / lift |
| **Correlated features** | `missed_payment_count` vs `loan_payment_ratio` (|r| = 0.84), `balance_trend` vs `salary_credit_frequency` (0.57) | filter selection drops one; permutation importance shares credit |
| **Outliers** | ~0.5 % of customers get one huge one-off credit (property sale / inheritance, up to 2.6 M) | `average_balance` long right tail; `log_average_balance`; trees are robust |
| **Late-arriving data** | `loan_status` published on day 5 of the next month | `available_at` + availability rule; `02_feature_manual_examples` shows one unpublished row inflating a feature |
| **Leakage columns** | `collections_status`, `recovery_amount`, `days_past_due` of future months, balance collapse after default | `04_leakage_demo` |
| **Sensitive / proxy attribute** | `segment` (and income-type features that act as proxies) | registry: `segment` Rejected; `01_data_profile` section 6 |
| **Data drift + rising default rate** | macro stress from 2023-09 | `11_drift_shifted`, `11c_label_lag_timeline` |
| **Data-quality failure** | `batch_dq_issue.csv` | `11b_drift_data_quality_issue` |
| **Label lag** | target known 6 months after as_of | `11c_label_lag_timeline`, `retrain.py` label maturity |

## 6. Default behaviour (what the model can learn)
A customer who will default shows warning signs before the default month: balance falls, card utilisation rises, salary gets irregular, instalments are missed (gradual type, ~76 % in calm times);
or the salary simply stops 4 months before (job-loss type, 12 % calm, ~50 % under stress); or nothing visible until three forced missed instalments (sudden type, 12 %).
~35 % of customers also go through a harmless "rough patch" (false alarm), so the task is not trivial.
In the default month the bank sweeps the account: balance collapses, salary stops, card is blocked, `collections_status` becomes `in_collections` and recoveries appear.
